name: פּוּעָה
gloss: girl; or one who cries out
summary: The second of the two Hebrew midwives who feared God and would not kill the boys at the king of Egypt's command. Her name's root is not certain. With ע for an older ġ it matches Ugaritic pġt, 'girl', which is also the name of a woman, Aqhat's sister. With the ע of the verb פָּעָה it would mean 'one who cries out', the verb Isaiah uses of a woman giving birth.

evidence.note: The name of the one was שִׁפְרָה, and the name of the second was פּוּעָה.
The root's one verb: כַּיּוֹלֵדָה אֶפְעֶה, like a woman giving birth I will cry out.

note: BDB files the name without a root (q.ap.ae, among the words of פון), and its פּוּ- is not a pattern the verb פָּעָה forms elsewhere in scripture, so its place under פעה rests on its consonants. The Issacharite Puah (פּוּאָה, פֻּוָּה; Gen 46:13, Num 26:23, Jdg 10:1, 1Ch 7:1) is a different spelling and not this name. Her story is Exo 1:15–21.
